adm.intro: One delta per current role and technology family. Changes are versioned and audited; publishing writes a ledger entry.
adm.rulesBody: Rank 1-6; one to seven distinct dimensions, each adapts or new, in English and Arabic; up to 8 catalogue skills at level 1-3; links only to existing training; at least two https sources to publish. Security, safeguards and cyber roles stay path-only. No headcount, site or deployment claims.

pl.intro: Walk through how a pressurised water reactor plant turns heat into electricity, and how it keeps the reaction controlled, the fuel cooled and radioactivity contained when something goes wrong.
pl.simBody: Everything on this page is a simplified illustration that runs in your browser. Values are illustrative indices from 0 to 100, never plant temperatures, pressures, setpoints or flows, and nothing you do here is stored.
pl.simNote: SIMULATED: an illustrative model for learning, not plant data or procedures.
pl.fnEyebrow: What every nuclear plant must always do

fnHelp.control: Keep the chain reaction under control and stop it when needed, for example by inserting the control rods.
fnHelp.cool: Remove heat from the fuel, including the decay heat that continues after shutdown.
fnHelp.contain: Keep radioactive material inside its barriers: the fuel, the primary circuit and the containment building.

tw.intro: Read simulated trends from a digital twin of a plant system, spend a limited check budget, name the degrading component and failure mode, then choose a conservative action and say why.
tw.simBody: Every system and trend here is synthetic (SYN-TW codes) and labelled SIMULATED. No plant data, setpoints or security details are used. Scoring is deterministic and explained.

list.title: Drills
list.intro: Each drill names the twin and plant-data skills it evidences.

scoring.title: How drills are scored
scoring.eyebrow: The same rules on the server and here
scoring.component: Right component: 4 points; right failure mode as well: 2 more.
scoring.checks: Each useful check: 1 point; each wasted check: minus 1.
scoring.action: Best action: 3 points; another conservative action: 2.
scoring.rationales: Each sound reason: 1 point; each unsound reason: minus 1.
scoring.unsafe: An unsafe check or action fails the drill whatever the score.
scoring.pass: Pass: safe, the right component, a conservative action and the pass mark.
scoring.level: Level 2 needs a level-2 drill, the right mode, every useful check, no wasted check and 85% or more.
scoring.latest: Your latest attempt on a drill replaces the evidence from earlier attempts.

reason.componentWrong: The component you named is not the one degrading.
reason.modeWrong: The failure mode is not right (it only scores with the right component).

action.best: You chose the best conservative action.
action.conservative: Your action is conservative, though not the best one.
action.not_conservative: Your action is not conservative enough.

reason.unsafe: An unsafe check or action fails the drill whatever the score.
reason.notPassed: Not passed: {pct}% against a pass mark of {pass}%, or a safety condition was not met.

twd.notFound: Drill not found or not open.
twd.task: Compare each trend with the model band (shaded). Then run up to your budget of checks: each one reveals a synthetic result.
twd.trendsEyebrow: Shaded band = what the twin model expects
twd.checksEyebrow: Choose carefully; some checks waste time and some are unsafe
twd.budgetUsed: Check budget used. Undo a check to choose another.
twd.actBody: When in doubt, choose the action that keeps margins and protection in place. Pick an action and up to three reasons for it.
twd.confirmBody: {checks} checks, component: {component}, action: {action}. The result is scored on the server.
twd.chartLabel: Simulated trend of {name} against the model band
twd.tableCaption: {name}: values by time; model band {lo} to {hi}

res.summary: {points} of {max} points · {useful} of {total} useful checks · {wasted} wasted
res.unsafe: An unsafe check or action fails the drill whatever the score. Review the explanation below.
res.evidenceWritten: Assessment evidence written at level {n} for:
res.noEvidence: No evidence was written: a drill writes evidence only when passed.

ttw.intro: The digital-twin drill bank and its results. Statistics use each person's latest attempt; groups under 10 are suppressed.
ttw.ruleBody: Drills use synthetic SYN-TW systems and SIMULATED trends, evidence at level 1 or 2, and no plant security wording. The server checks every drill before saving.
ttw.statsDesc: Latest attempt per person and drill; cells under {min} people are suppressed.
ttw.noStats: Results are for training staff and HR.
ttw.bankDesc: Every drill with its key where you may read it.
ttw.bankDescEdit: Every drill with its key. Edit, duplicate or publish a drill.
ttw.keyHidden: The answer key is visible to the training manager.
ttw.structureHint: series, components, modes, checks, actions, rationales and key, as in the existing drills.
ttw.confirmPublish: The drill will be published for staff. Its key stays visible to training staff only.
ttw.confirmDraft: The drill will be saved as a draft that staff cannot see.

problem.texts: Fill every title, summary, scenario and system text in English and Arabic.

problem.skill: Choose 1 to 3 twin or plant-data skills.
problem.series: Trends need 6 to 48 time points and 2 to 6 signals with a valid model band.
problem.components: 3 to 6 components with English and Arabic labels.
problem.checks: 3 to 8 checks with minutes and English and Arabic results.
problem.max_checks: The check budget must be between 1 and the number of checks.
problem.key: The key must name a listed component, mode, checks, conservative best action and 1 to 3 sound reasons.
